Diagnoses and fixes a reward-hacking failure mode (spurious advantage from guessing) in GRPO-style RL with verifiable rewards, including search agents where many rollout paths satisfy the same verifiable check -- directly analogous to training hexgen via a frozen machine-checkable verifier over best-of-N candidate programs, relevant to verifier-in-the-loop training design.

payload.problem_addressed: GRPO's within-group advantage estimator assigns a rollout the same high gradient magnitude whether it reached the correct answer by genuine reasoning or by guessing, which the authors call the 'spurious advantage'; this is largest in bounded-answer tasks, bounded sub-cases hidden inside open-answer training sets, and multi-turn search agents where many distinct rollouts land on the same verified outcome.
payload.method_summary: SignBalance replaces GRPO's composition-dependent advantage with a magnitude that keeps only the verifier sign, uses a constant global scale c for correct/incorrect classes, and restores batch-level zero-mean force balance via a stop-gradient per-class rescaling (A+=c, A-=-c*sg[n+/n-]); it is a drop-in, parameter-free (apart from c) replacement inside the standard PPO-style clipped GRPO surrogate.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper identifies a spurious-advantage failure mode in the GRPO advantage estimator that rewards lucky guesses as much as genuine reasoning whenever a task's effective answer surface is finite. It characterizes three cases where this becomes sizeable (bounded-answer tasks, bounded sub-cases within nominally open-answer sets such as 55.95% of MATH-7.5K, and multi-turn search agents with outcome-only reward) and proposes SignBalance, an advantage estimator whose per-rollout magnitude is independent of within-group composition. Experiments across math reasoning (0.5B and 3B Qwen models) and multi-turn search-agent QA (7B) show SignBalance matches GRPO on open-answer math while giving consistent, sustained gains on bounded-answer math and search-agent benchmarks.
key_architecture_choices: per-class (correct/incorrect) separate normalization as an intermediate step
sign-only global-scale magnitude c decoupled from within-group counts
stop-gradient per-class rescaling to restore batch-level zero-mean force balance
drop-in replacement inside the unchanged PPO-style clipped surrogate, no extra model or inference cost
payload.headline_results: At 0.5B scale SignBalance improves SAT-Math from 65.62 to 71.88 (+6.26) and AQuA from 29.53 to 35.43 (+5.90) over GRPO while matching it on open-answer math (Avg-8 34.24 to 36.61 overall gain +2.37); at 3B scale it attains the best Avg-8 (43.78, leading 7/8 benchmarks); on multi-turn search-agent QA it attains the best Avg-6 (37.80, +1.80 over Search-R1).
claimed_advantages: parameter-free apart from a single global scale c
no external model or added inference-time cost
leaves the PPO-style clipped surrogate unchanged, a one-line advantage substitution
removes the guess-driven gradient component identified as the spurious advantage
limitations: validation does not yet extend beyond math reasoning and multi-turn search-agent QA to more general settings such as finite tool-selection agents
has not quantitatively measured whether the policy's reasoning ability/confidence actually improves, only downstream task accuracy
shows a small tradeoff loss on MATH-500 relative to GRPO

payload.applicability_to_our_problem: hexgen's proposed training regime (best-of-N candidate programs screened by a frozen, machine-checkable verifier) is structurally the finite/bounded-answer-surface + search-agent case this paper analyzes: many distinct DSL programs can pass the identical verifier check, so if hexgen is ever trained with GRPO-style RL against the verifier's pass/fail signal (rather than only supervised imitation + best-of-N filtering), a standard GRPO advantage would over-reward rollouts that pass the verifier by chance (e.g. degenerate or memorized command sequences) as much as genuinely well-formed programs. SignBalance's composition-independent, sign-based advantage with per-class force balance is a directly transferable one-line fix to avoid this reward-hacking-like failure mode in verifier-in-the-loop RL fine-tuning of the graph-transformer decoder.
payload.reviewer_notes: Caveat: this is anticipatory value, not immediately applicable, since hexgen's current recipe is supervised imitation on inverse-factory + auto-labeled real parts with best-of-N verifier screening at inference, not GRPO-style policy-gradient RL. The multi-turn search-agent case (many action sequences reaching the same correct final answer) is the closest structural analogy to autoregressive program generation where many token sequences can compile to a verifier-passing mesh. Worth keeping on file for if/when the roadmap adds RLVR-style fine-tuning against the frozen verifier.

payload.problem_addressed: Specialized CAD generation models are trained on narrow input domains (renders or text only) and generalize poorly to real industrial design intent, while general-purpose frontier models cover broad inputs but perform inconsistently on CAD; both part-level generation (mapping multimodal intent to an executable CAD DSL program) and assembly-level generation (mating relations, pose estimation, multi-part placement) remain hard.
payload.method_summary: VisCAD-M1 is a 27B multimodal model trained with a three-stage pipeline (large-scale mid-training on ~1M reversibly-constructed CAD-program/multi-view-image pairs, robust SFT on ~150k noisy industrial product images with multi-candidate teacher distillation, and continual high-quality SFT on ~10k curated generate-verify-feedback examples) to map text/drawings/photos/renders to executable FreeCAD Python programs; a parallel test-time-scaling (parallel-tts) step reuses the model itself as a listwise reranker/verifier over k rollouts. VisCAD-H1 is a separate CAD-native agentic harness that decomposes assembly intent into a DSL-agnostic intermediate representation (BoM, per-part IR, mating/placement) gated at each stage before backend code realization.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper presents VisCAD, a foundation model suite for industrial CAD: VisCAD-M1 (27B), which achieves the best part-level profile-average score among evaluated models on PubCADBench/RealCADBench (0.5540 vs. 0.5496 for the best frontier model), rising to 0.5797 with self-reranking test-time scaling; and VisCAD-H1, a domain-specific assembly harness that scores 85.0 on an assembly judge versus 68.0 (Codex) and 52.0 (Claude Code). It also contributes a data-curation pipeline unifying heterogeneous CAD data into intent-program-shape triples and a multi-stage training recipe.
key_architecture_choices: 27B multimodal encoder-decoder generating executable FreeCAD Python from text/drawings/photos/renders

three-stage training: mid-training (syntax/coverage) -> robust SFT (domain-gap bridging via multi-candidate teacher distillation) -> continual high-quality SFT (geometric fidelity via generate-verify-feedback)
parallel test-time scaling: model reused as its own listwise reranker/verifier over multiple rollouts, shown to beat sequential self-refinement
DSL-agnostic intermediate representation (BoM + per-part IR + mating/placement) as a portability layer across FreeCAD/Fusion/SolidWorks for the assembly harness
four-gated agentic assembly pipeline: multimodal understanding & BoM -> parallel per-part IR -> global IR review -> CAD realization

metrics: Profile Average (equal-weight mean of the four)
Assembly Judge score (component geometry, assembly accuracy, system design)
payload.headline_results: VisCAD-M1 reaches profile-average 0.5540 vs. 0.5496 for the strongest frontier baseline (Gemini-3.1-Pro), improving to 0.5797 with parallel test-time scaling (k=16); VisCAD-H1 scores 85.0 on the assembly judge vs. 68.0 for Codex and 52.0 for Claude Code on a 50-instance study.
claimed_advantages: broader modality coverage (text, 2D drawings, real product photos, renders) than prior specialized CAD models which mostly use one modality
self-verification via parallel-tts improves final program quality without additional training
DSL-agnostic IR lets the same assembly plan be realized in multiple CAD backends (FreeCAD, Fusion, SolidWorks) with higher stability than a general coding agent
limitations: judge scores on some slices (e.g. 2D drawings, BenchCAD, CADBench) trail frontier general-purpose models even where IoU leads, showing geometry and visual-semantic identity can diverge
sequential self-refinement test-time scaling did not help, only parallel reranking did
assembly-level integration with part-level model (VisCAD-M1 + VisCAD-H1) is still a stated future direction, not yet unified
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: Several mechanisms transfer directly to hexgen: (1) parallel test-time scaling, using the model itself as a listwise reranker/verifier over multiple best-of-N rollouts, is directly analogous to hexgen's best-of-N + frozen verifier screening and suggests a learned reranker could be layered on top of or in place of hand-coded verifier checks to break ties among verifier-passing candidates; (2) the three-stage training curriculum (syntax/coverage mid-training -> noisy-domain robust SFT with multi-candidate distillation -> high-quality generate-verify-feedback fine-tuning) is a template for combining hexgen's inverse-factory synthetic data with auto-labeled real CAD parts while explicitly targeting the synthetic-to-real domain gap; (3) the DSL-agnostic intermediate representation for assembly generation is a reusable pattern for representing an hex-mesh program independent of mesher backend syntax, and the staged gating (syntax-valid per-part IR before anything is treated as a solid) parallels grammar/constrained decoding for structural validity.
payload.reviewer_notes: VisCAD targets general parametric CAD program generation (FreeCAD Python) rather than hex-meshing DSLs specifically, and its verifier is a self-reranking judge model rather than a hard machine-checkable compile/mesh-quality check like hexgen's; the domain-gap-bridging role of 'robust SFT' (noisy real photos, multi-candidate teacher distillation) is the most directly reusable idea for hexgen's real-CAD auto-labeled data. No training/inference code appears to be released.
payload.implementation_cost_estimate: M -- the parallel-tts self-reranking idea is a moderate-effort addition to an existing best-of-N + verifier pipeline; the full three-stage training curriculum and DSL-agnostic IR would be a larger (L) undertaking to replicate from scratch

payload.problem_addressed: Existing CAD benchmarks mostly emphasize synthetic or CAD-native settings, limited input modalities, or executability/IoU alone, so they conflate distinct failure modes (a program can execute yet omit mounting holes, or look plausible in a render yet misplace assembly components); evaluating real industrial intent-to-CAD-program generation requires separating executability, geometric fidelity, and visual-semantic identity.
payload.method_summary: RealCADBench curates 12,632 tasks across 19 factory-automation categories spanning text, 2D engineering drawings, real product pictures, and rendered images, for both Part and Assembly modeling, all under one shared FreeCAD-API artifact contract (the runtime executes the generated Python and exports result.stl; only the exported model is scored). It reports a 1,770-task evaluation slice (1,745 Part tasks across four regimes plus RCB-Assm25, a stratified 25-task assembly study) and evaluates nine frontier models plus two general-purpose coding agents (Codex+GPT-5.5, Claude Code+Claude Opus 4.8) using four metrics: executability, Solid IoU, Surface IoU, and a rubric-based visual-semantic identity Judge, combined into a Profile Average.
payload.contributions_summary: The paper introduces RealCADBench, a large real-industrial-intent CAD benchmark spanning four input modalities and both part and assembly modeling with a shared FreeCAD execution contract. It proposes an evaluation protocol beyond executability/IoU that adds a rubric-based visual-semantic identity Judge, and reports a comparative study showing no single frontier model or agent leads all four metrics, that difficulty ordering shifts across input regimes, and that agentic execution-and-repair loops can trade off geometric IoU gains against loss of visual-semantic identity.
key_architecture_choices: shared FreeCAD-Python artifact contract: score only the executed/exported solid, not the code path

four-metric protocol: executability, Solid IoU, Surface IoU (via deterministic signed-PCA-aligned voxel occupancy), and a rubric-based visual-semantic Judge (frozen Kimi K2.6 protocol) that never sees the reference model
Profile Average = equal-weight mean of executability + Solid IoU + Surface IoU + Judge/100

staged reference construction: multi-system candidate proposal, screening, and CAD-expert verification (only ~17% of candidates accepted) to obtain trustworthy ground-truth references for real/photo/drawing/text tasks
agent-vs-standalone-model comparison design: evaluates general coding agents (Codex, Claude Code) as complete methods against their own paired base models on identical tasks
datasets: RealCADBench (12,632 total tasks; 1,745-task Part slice across Text/2D-Drawing/Real-Picture/Rendered-Image; RCB-Assm25 25-task stratified assembly slice)
payload.headline_results: No frontier model leads all four metrics: Gemini-3.1-Pro-Preview has the best regime-balanced Profile Average (0.5507), GPT-5.5 leads executability (0.9311) and Judge (73.79), Kimi K3 leads both IoU metrics despite only 34.22% executability. Rendered-image inputs lead every metric among the four Part regimes. On RCB-Assm25, Codex+GPT-5.5 improves executability (+0.16) and both IoUs over standalone GPT-5.5 but lowers the Judge by 6.98 points, leaving standalone GPT-5.5 as Judge leader.
claimed_advantages: separates executability, geometric fidelity, and visual-semantic identity as distinct axes rather than one aggregate score, exposing failure modes a single metric would hide
covers realistic, noisy industrial design intent (real photos, engineering drawings) rather than only synthetic/CAD-native data
evaluates agentic execute-and-repair harnesses as complete methods, showing the harness can trade IoU gains for identity/Judge losses
limitations: current release is a 1,770-task evaluation slice, not yet the full 12,632-task benchmark (full public release is future work)
text-regime references and Judge inputs are derived from the paired real-picture case via Gemini generation/validation rather than independent ground truth
reference construction and screening pipeline (17% acceptance) is labor-intensive (CAD-expert verification) and may not scale directly
recurring failure modes noted: missing fine structures, loss of part identity, incorrect assembly placement
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: This is close kin to hexgen's own evaluation design: RealCADBench's core lesson -- that executability alone is a poor proxy for structural/geometric fidelity and that different axes (compiles/executes vs. geometric IoU vs. semantic identity) can rank systems differently -- directly supports hexgen's multi-criterion frozen verifier (compiles, zero inverted elements, scaled-Jacobian/aspect-ratio bounds, surface-match fidelity, feature-edge capture, element-budget sanity) rather than a single pass/fail signal. Its shared-runtime, score-only-the-executed-artifact protocol, its staged reference-verification pipeline (candidate proposal -> screening -> expert acceptance, ~17% accept rate) for building trustworthy (B-rep, program) ground truth from noisy real industrial CAD assets, and its finding that agentic execute-and-repair harnesses trade IoU for structural/identity correctness are all directly transferable to how hexgen should construct and validate its real-CAD auto-labeled training/eval data and interpret verifier-passing-but-low-quality outputs.
payload.reviewer_notes: Produced by the same team as the VisCAD paper (2609.03811) and used as one of VisCAD's evaluation benchmarks; the two should be read together. RealCADBench targets general parametric CAD (FreeCAD Python) rather than hex-meshing specifically, and its 'verifier' is a learned visual-semantic Judge rather than hexgen's hard geometric/mesh-quality checks, but the benchmark-design lessons (multi-axis evaluation, executability != quality) transfer directly.
